national_raw_news.content: BRICS leaders have stressed that energy security is a crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations. During the two day BRICS summit held in New Delhi, the member nations highlighted the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and protection of critical energy infrastructure. During the Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi cautioned that the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could become a hurdle to progress. India hosted the summit under the theme Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, placing people-centred development and the interests of the Global South at the heart of its presidency. The most significant outcome of the BRICS summit was the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration, which outlined the shared position on major geopolitical and economic issues. On the situation in West Asia, BRICS leaders called for maximum restraint, dialogue and diplomacy, and stressed the need to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure. The leaders strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and reiterated their commitment to a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism. A consensus was reached on a ‘BRICS Integrated Early Warning System’ for the prevention of and response to infectious diseases. This summit was highly significant from the perspective of global politics, the economy, and multilateral cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: 43 mins ago | Regional News 36 China significantly reduces troop deployment in 2025, says Defence Ministry report
national_raw_news.content: Government has said that the security situation in Jammu and Kashmir remains firmly under control due to the relentless efforts of the army. In its latest annual report 2025-26, the Defence Ministry said that these efforts have led to a significant decline in violence, a reduction in protests, and zero incidents of stone pelting. According to the report, the situation within Jammu and Kashmir and along the Line of Control had significantly altered during Operation Sindoor. However, after the Director Generals of Military Operations level talks last year, the situation has stabilised to a large extent, though the unpredictability continues. The report also highlighted the overall situation with China. The year 2025 witnessed a significant reduction in the deployment of China’s People Liberation Army (PLA) Forces opposite the Northern Borders, with 10 Combined Arms Brigade-sized forces each deployed in areas along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and in traditional training areas. The bilateral interactions between India and China at political, diplomatic and military levels facilitated positive developments along the Northern Borders, leading to stability. According to the report, the deployment of the Indian Army in all sectors along the LAC is robust, well-poised, and prepared to deal with any emerging contingency. The report also highlighted that the Defence Ministry is actively prioritizing the Indian industrial base to reduce dependency on foreign imports. Accordingly, a significant portion of the defence expenditure is directed inward boosting the local economy and defence infrastructure. Out of Total Defence Procurement approximately 75 percent was spent specifically for domestic procurement.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 320 PM Modi thanks BRICS leaders for productive and outcome-oriented Delhi summit
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed gratitude to the leaders of all the BRICS member countries for making the Delhi summit of the grouping productive and outcome-oriented. A video reflecting key moments of the two-day summit was posted on the social media handles of the prime minister. In the video, a part of the prime minister’s summit speech was shown where he said through BRICS, India has advanced friendship, partnership and cooperation all across. The leaders who attended the summit included Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Philippines Ferdinand R Marcos Jr, Uganda’s Vice President Jessica Alupo, besides others, also attended the summit. India hosted the BRICS Summit on September 12-13 and it was attended by the leaders of the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries of the grouping, besides some international organisations. Mr Modi also held 15 sit-down bilateral meetings with heads of states or heads of governments in the last three days on the sidelines of the summit.

national_raw_news.title: India wins record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title, President Murmu congratulates team 7 hours ago 244
national_raw_news.content: India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament. India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match. India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours. Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has congratulated the Indian women’s cricket team via a social media post. Mr Birla lauded the team for remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament and securing victory in the Asia Cup for the 8th time. He added that the cricketers gave a splendid demonstration of their talent and determination in the tournament and this victory is a triumph of the strength, hard work, and dreams of the daughters of India. The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that the accomplishment inspires the youth of the country, to dream big, work hard, and move forward with full determination to achieve their goals.
